item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q014_paper_example_reclassification_pa1492","answer":"In SCOP 1.69, PA1492 from PDB 1t1j chain A was domain d1t1ja_ / SUNID 106249, classified as c.137.1.1: class c, Alpha and beta proteins (a/b); its own Hypothetical protein PA1492 fold c.137 / SUNID 110459; PA1492 superfamily c.137.1 / SUNID 110460; and PA1492 family c.137.1.1 / SUNID 110461. Nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase from 1f8y chain A was d1f8ya_ / SUNID 31395 in the different Flavodoxin-like fold c.23 / SUNID 52171, N-deoxyribosyltransferase superfamily c.23.14 / SUNID 52309, and N-deoxyribosyltransferase family c.23.14.1 / SUNID 52310. Thus in SCOP 1.69 the two domains shared only the broad alpha/beta class c; that old classification did not assert a fold-level match or an evolutionary relationship between PA1492 and the 1f8y enzyme.\n\nIn the current SCOPe release, 2.08, the real PA1492 coordinates were renamed to d1t1ja1 and moved into the same Flavodoxin-like fold and the same N-(deoxy)ribosyltransferase-like superfamily as d1f8ya_: d1t1ja1 is c.23.14.2, with family SUNID 110461 still named Hypothetical protein PA1492, while d1f8ya_ remains c.23.14.1, the N-deoxyribosyltransferase family. The relationship therefore changed from “same class only” to “same superfamily, different families”: SCOPe now treats PA1492 and nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase as probable homologs in superfamily c.23.14 / SUNID 52309, but it does not merge PA1492 into the enzymatically characterized N-deoxyribosyltransferase family c.23.14.1 or transfer the 1f8y substrate/active-site function to PA1492 at family strength. The 2.08 1t1j chain record also contains a synthetic l.1.1.1 tag sentinel d1t1ja2 at A:0-0; that is not the PA1492 structural domain and should not be used as the reclassified
